Situation1: There is a scheduled family gathering on the calendar.
Expectation2: Secure packages and confirm successful delivery
Situation2: Leaving a package safely at the doorstep when no one is home
Story:
I glanced at the clock, my heart fluttering with anticipation. Today was the family gathering I’d been looking forward to all week—my daughter promised to bring the grandkids, and I’d baked their favorite cookies. The house was filled with the scent of cinnamon and laughter echoed in my mind, even before anyone arrived. But just as I was setting the table, my phone buzzed. A last-minute delivery assignment popped up on my app: a package needed to be dropped off across town, and the customer had left strict instructions to ensure it was placed safely at the doorstep, out of sight.

I stared at the message, feeling the weight of both worlds pressing in. My family expected me to be present, to share stories and hugs, to be the grandparent who never missed a moment. But my job demanded reliability—packages couldn’t wait, and customers counted on me to deliver, no matter what. My hands trembled as I weighed the disappointment I might cause at home against the trust placed in me by my employer. The clock ticked louder, and I stood frozen, torn between two lives that suddenly felt impossible to balance.
